controls.label: Query matrix Q
controls.help: Changing an entry of Q changes the score matrix, and therefore changes the weights, row sums and output.

controls.label: Key matrix K
controls.help: Changing an entry of K changes the score matrix, which changes the weights and the output.

controls.label: Value matrix V
controls.help: Changing an entry of V changes the output directly and leaves the score matrix, weights and row sums unchanged.

controls.label: Divide scores by sqrt(dk)
controls.help: Turning this off removes the 1/sqrt(dk) division, which changes the score matrix, the weights and the output; the row sums stay at 1.

explorations.title: Equal scores give uniform attention
explorations.instruction: Predict: when both scores in a row are equal, what will the two attention weights in that row be? Then apply the preset, which sets Q to [[1,0],[1,0]], K to [[1,0],[1,0]], V to [[1,0],[0,1]] and turns the 1/sqrt(dk) scaling on.
explorations.observe: The weights heatmap shows 0.5 in all four cells. The row sums readouts show 1 and 1. The output heatmap shows 0.5 in all four cells.
explorations.why: Every score is 1 before scaling and 1/sqrt(2) after, but all entries in a row are equal, and the softmax of equal values always gives 0.5 and 0.5. Each output row is therefore the average of value rows (1,0) and (0,1), which is (0.5,0.5).

explorations.title: A dominant score concentrates one row
explorations.instruction: Predict: when scaling is off and query row 0 is (2,0), what weights will row 0 get? Then apply the preset, which sets Q to [[2,0],[0,1]], K to [[2,0],[0,1]], V to [[1,0],[0,1]] and turns the 1/sqrt(dk) scaling off.
explorations.observe: The score matrix row 0 is 4 and 0, and row 1 is 0 and 1. The weights heatmap row 0 is about 0.982 and 0.018, while row 1 is about 0.269 and 0.731. The row sums readouts are 1 and 1. The output heatmap row 0 is about 0.982 and 0.018.
explorations.why: Without the 1/sqrt(dk) division the score 4 stays large, so exp(4) dominates exp(0) in row 0 and the softmax places most of the weight on key 0. Row 1 has scores 0 and 1, so its weights stay closer to even, and both rows still sum to 1.
